dimensions.originality: Distinctive reader-facing angle not already carried by the existing ten articles
dimensions.reader_value: Immediate value to a reader who does not know the repository
dimensions.evidence_maturity: How much current source material can support without new retrieval
dimensions.narrative_potential: Whether the material has tension, movement and a non-list argument
dimensions.writing_readiness: How close the material is to a complete manuscript with current sources
dimensions.claim_safety: Ease of preserving the existing claim ceiling in readable prose
dimensions.overlap_safety: 5 means low duplication risk with the existing publication corpus

ranked_candidates.working_title: 一个系统如何在停止时仍然诚实：把开放义务从任务生命周期里拆出来
ranked_candidates.selection_reason: Task142 supplies a concrete lifecycle change: formal task terminality and obligation liveness are independent. This is narrower and more original than repeating the general receipt-versus-reality warning.
ranked_candidates.claim_ceiling: Repository-local lifecycle semantics and engineering evidence only; no external completion, executor capability or production readiness.

ranked_candidates.working_title: 树冠会降温吗：一个好问题如何被证据层拆开
ranked_candidates.selection_reason: A concrete public-source question lets a general reader watch useful evidence survive while the causal sentence is narrowed. It is more accessible than a second abstract essay about representation.
ranked_candidates.claim_ceiling: Named observational materials support a bounded canopy/near-ground-air-temperature association; no city-wide causal tree-planting effect and no direct human heat-stress result.

ranked_candidates.working_title: 资源托举为什么会变成路径控制
ranked_candidates.selection_reason: This is the required substantive non-meta piece. Its lower evidence score is deliberate: the article will make the unresolved status part of the argument and will name counterexamples rather than hide the gap.
ranked_candidates.claim_ceiling: Pointfire-originated candidate model and writing problem; no universal causal law, measured prevalence or external validation.
